# Acceptance Criteria

Status: draft

## AC-1: Galaxy Map Displays Star Systems

**Derived from:** UC-1
**Verifies:** FR-1

Scenario: Player views the galaxy map with all star systems
  Given a new or loaded game is in progress
  And the player is docked at a station
  When the player opens the galaxy map view
  Then at least 8 named star systems are displayed
  And each displayed system indicates it has a station
  And the player's current location is indicated

---

## AC-2: New Game Starting Conditions

**Derived from:** UC-2
**Verifies:** FR-10, RULE-1

Scenario: Player begins a new game with correct initial state
  Given the player starts a new game
  When the game initializes
  Then the player has exactly 100 credits
  And the player's cargo hold is at a defined small capacity
  And the player is docked at a station

---

## AC-3: Buy Commodities with Sufficient Resources

**Derived from:** UC-2
**Verifies:** FR-2

Scenario: Player successfully purchases commodities
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient credits
  And the player's cargo hold has available capacity
  When the player selects a commodity and quantity to buy
  Then the commodity is added to the player's cargo
  And the player's credits are reduced by the total purchase price

---

## AC-4: Buy Rejected with Insufficient Credits

**Derived from:** UC-2
**Verifies:** FR-2

Scenario: Purchase fails when credits are insufficient
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player's credits are less than the total purchase price
  When the player attempts to buy a commodity
  Then the purchase is rejected
  And the player's credits and cargo are unchanged

---

## AC-5: Buy Rejected When Cargo Capacity Exceeded

**Derived from:** UC-2
**Verifies:** FR-2, RULE-6

Scenario: Purchase fails when it would exceed cargo capacity
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient credits
  And the player's current cargo plus the requested quantity would exceed cargo capacity
  When the player attempts to buy the commodity
  Then the purchase is rejected
  And the player's credits and cargo are unchanged

```yaml
properties:
  cargo_bounds:
    description: "Total cargo quantity never exceeds capacity"
    invariant: "cargo_quantity + purchase_quantity <= cargo_capacity"
    property_type: bounds
  rejection_idempotency:
    description: "A rejected purchase leaves all state unchanged"
    invariant: "state_after_rejected_buy == state_before_rejected_buy"
    property_type: idempotency
```

---

## AC-6: Sell Commodities and Accumulate Profit

**Derived from:** UC-2
**Verifies:** FR-2, RULE-3

Scenario: Player sells commodities and profit is tracked
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player holds commodities in cargo purchased at a known buy price
  When the player sells the commodity at the station's market price
  Then the player's credits increase by the total sell price
  And the commodity is removed from cargo
  And accumulated profit increases by the difference between sell price and buy price

```yaml
properties:
  profit_positivity:
    description: "Profit from a single trade is non-negative when sell price >= buy price"
    invariant: "profit_per_unit >= 0 when sell_price >= buy_price"
    property_type: positivity
  profit_monotonicity:
    description: "Accumulated profit never decreases"
    invariant: "accumulated_profit_after >= accumulated_profit_before"
    property_type: monotonicity
  credits_conservation:
    description: "Credits change exactly by the transaction delta"
    invariant: "credits_after = credits_before - buy_total + sell_total"
    property_type: identity
```

---

## AC-7: Hyperspace Jump Consumes Fuel Proportional to Distance

**Derived from:** UC-3
**Verifies:** FR-3, RULE-2

Scenario: Player jumps to another system and fuel is consumed
  Given the player is docked at a station with sufficient fuel
  And the player has selected a destination system
  When the player initiates a hyperspace jump
  Then fuel is deducted proportional to the distance between origin and destination
  And the player arrives in the destination system

```yaml
properties:
  fuel_positivity:
    description: "Fuel consumed is always positive for any valid jump"
    invariant: "fuel_consumed > 0 when distance > 0"
    property_type: positivity
  fuel_proportionality:
    description: "Fuel consumed increases with distance"
    invariant: "fuel_consumed(distance_a) <= fuel_consumed(distance_b) when distance_a <= distance_b"
    property_type: monotonicity
  fuel_identity:
    description: "Zero-distance jump consumes zero fuel"
    invariant: "fuel_consumed(0) = 0"
    property_type: identity
```

---

## AC-8: Hyperspace Jump Prevented with Insufficient Fuel

**Derived from:** UC-3
**Verifies:** FR-3, RULE-2

Scenario: Jump fails when fuel is below the required amount
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player's current fuel is less than the fuel required for the selected destination
  When the player attempts to initiate a hyperspace jump
  Then the jump is prevented
  And the player's fuel remains unchanged
  And the player's location remains unchanged

```yaml
properties:
  fuel_guard:
    description: "No fuel is deducted when the jump is prevented"
    invariant: "fuel_after == fuel_before when fuel_before < fuel_required"
    property_type: identity
  location_guard:
    description: "Player location is unchanged when jump is prevented"
    invariant: "location_after == location_before when fuel_before < fuel_required"
    property_type: identity
```

---

## AC-9: Pirate Encounter Presents Choices

**Derived from:** UC-4
**Verifies:** FR-4

Scenario: Player encounters a pirate after a hyperspace jump
  Given the player has completed a hyperspace jump
  And a pirate encounter is triggered
  When the encounter is presented
  Then the player is given the option to fight or flee

---

## AC-10: Combat Resolves in Victory, Defeat, or Escape

**Derived from:** UC-5
**Verifies:** FR-5

Scenario: Combat ends with one of three outcomes
  Given the player is in ship-to-ship combat with an enemy
  When combat concludes
  Then the outcome is one of: victory (enemy destroyed), defeat (player destroyed), or escape (player disengages)

---

## AC-11: Enemy Destroyed Increments Kill Count

**Derived from:** UC-5
**Verifies:** FR-5, RULE-4

Scenario: Destroying an enemy ship updates the kill count
  Given the player is in combat with an enemy ship
  When the enemy ship is destroyed
  Then the player's combat kill count increases by exactly one
  And the kill contributes to Elite rating progression

```yaml
properties:
  kill_monotonicity:
    description: "Kill count never decreases"
    invariant: "kill_count_after >= kill_count_before"
    property_type: monotonicity
  kill_increment:
    description: "Each destroy event increments kills by exactly one"
    invariant: "kill_count_after = kill_count_before + 1"
    property_type: identity
```

---

## AC-12: Purchase Ship Upgrades with Sufficient Credits

**Derived from:** UC-6
**Verifies:** FR-6

Scenario: Player buys a ship upgrade
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the station offers ship upgrades
  And the player has sufficient credits for the selected upgrade
  When the player purchases an upgrade
  Then the player's credits are reduced by the upgrade cost
  And the upgraded ship attribute reflects the new capacity or power level

---

## AC-13: Upgrade Purchase Rejected with Insufficient Credits

**Derived from:** UC-6
**Verifies:** FR-6

Scenario: Upgrade purchase fails when credits are insufficient
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player's credits are less than the cost of the selected upgrade
  When the player attempts to purchase the upgrade
  Then the purchase is rejected
  And the player's credits and ship attributes are unchanged

---

## AC-14: Elite Rating Progresses Based on Profit and Kills

**Derived from:** UC-7
**Verifies:** FR-7, RULE-5

Scenario: Player's rating updates as profit and kills accumulate
  Given the player has completed trading transactions and combat engagements
  When the system evaluates the player's accumulated profit and kill count
  Then the player's rating tier reflects the combined evaluation
  And the rating is displayed on the HUD

```yaml
properties:
  rating_monotonicity:
    description: "Rating tier never decreases as profit or kills increase"
    invariant: "rating_tier(profit_after, kills_after) >= rating_tier(profit_before, kills_before) when profit_after >= profit_before and kills_after >= kills_before"
    property_type: monotonicity
```

---

## AC-15: Save and Load Restores Exact Game State

**Derived from:** UC-8
**Verifies:** FR-8

Scenario: Player saves and later loads a game
  Given a game is in progress with a known state
  When the player saves the game
  Then the game state is persisted
  When the player later loads the saved game
  Then the restored game state matches the saved state exactly

---

## AC-16: Health Check Endpoint Returns Success

**Derived from:** UC-9
**Verifies:** FR-9

Scenario: Factory operator verifies server is operational
  Given the game server has been started
  When a request is sent to the health check endpoint
  Then a success response is returned indicating the server is operational

---

## AC-17: Visual Effects Rendered for Each Gameplay Phase

**Derived from:** UC-10
**Verifies:** FR-11

Scenario: Player observes visual effects during gameplay
  Given the game is running in the browser
  When the player is in space navigation
  Then a parallax starfield is rendered
  When the player initiates a hyperspace jump
  Then a hyperspace jump visual effect plays
  When the player docks at a station
  Then a docking screen is displayed
  When the player is in normal gameplay
  Then a HUD showing shields, fuel, cargo, and credits is visible
  When the player is in combat
  Then laser fire and visual effects for hits and explosions are rendered

---

## AC-18: Game Renders at Target Frame Rate

**Derived from:** UC-10
**Verifies:** NFR-1

Scenario: Rendering performance meets the 60fps target
  Given the game is running on a 2020-era laptop in Google Chrome
  When the player is in normal gameplay including parallax starfield and combat effects
  Then the game renders at a target of 60 frames per second

---

## AC-19: Game Operates Fully Offline

**Derived from:** UC-10
**Verifies:** NFR-2

Scenario: No external network requests occur during gameplay
  Given the game has been installed and started
  When the game is running in the browser
  Then no external CDN dependencies are loaded
  And no network requests are made at runtime

---

## AC-20: Unit Tests Cover Core Logic

**Derived from:** UC-2
**Verifies:** NFR-4

Scenario: Unit tests validate core game logic
  Given the project source code is available
  When the test suite is run
  Then tests pass covering market pricing logic
  And tests pass covering jump and fuel consumption math
  And tests pass covering combat resolution
  And tests pass covering save and load serialization

---

## AC-21: Browser Smoke Test Verifies Canvas Rendering

**Derived from:** UC-10
**Verifies:** NFR-5

Scenario: Smoke test confirms the game canvas renders
  Given the game server is running
  When the browser smoke test is executed
  Then the game page loads successfully
  And the canvas element renders without errors

---

## AC-22: Game Playable After Install and Start

**Derived from:** UC-9
**Verifies:** NFR-6

Scenario: Game starts with zero manual build steps
  Given a clean checkout of the project
  When the operator runs install and start
  Then the game is immediately playable in the browser
  And no manual build, bundle, or compilation step was required

---
